The Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index, a closely watched gauge of American consumer confidence, registered at 51 in August, down from 54.5 in July. The reading came in well below the forecast of 54.5, signaling that households are feeling more pessimistic about the economic outlook. The drop reflects growing concerns among households about the economy, inflation, and personal finances.

Consumer sentiment fell 8% in August compared to last month, according to preliminary data from the University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers. Released Friday, the latest sentiment reading ended two consecutive months of improvement as Americans feel the effects of the Iran war pushing up fuel, energy and food prices.

The Current Economic Conditions Index increased to 54.8. This represents a 14.9% increase from the previous month but a 19.4% drop from a year ago. The latest reading was higher than the forecast of 54.9.

### Consumer Expectations Index (CEI)

The Consumer Expectations Index rose for a second straight month to 55.4. This represents a 9.3% increase from the previous month but a 4.0% drop from one year ago. The latest reading was higher than the forecast of 54.0.
